summary.headline: Sundram Fasteners FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR 5,612 crore and PAT hit a record INR 580 crore, helped by Q4 EBITDA margin of 17%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 5,612 crore (up from INR 5,231 crore) and profit before exceptional items of INR 750 crore (up 12% from INR 668 crore). Exceptional items included a full reversal of a prior impairment provision, partly offset by an INR 11 crore gratuity provision under the new Labour Code. Q4 saw exports return to growth in both USD and INR terms, and EBITDA margin widened to 17% from 15.6% a year earlier. Management said April started well and that it targets double-digit growth over the next two years.

financial_highlights.change: Highest in company history; INR 577 crore after MTM vs INR 517 crore
Stated for the quarter/year as per call; treat with caution
Crossed INR 1,500 crore for first time; includes exchange gains
YoY, on stable RM and absence of one-time Q4 FY25 costs
Q4 grew in USD and INR terms; rupee weakened about 4%

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Management cited OE as very strong, with growth of about 13% expected in FY27 for the segment. Growth in FY26 was driven by OE and retail.

segments.name: Retail / aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retail grew close to 20% YoY in Q4. Management projects about 15% retail growth in FY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports fell about 8%, attributed to tariffs and geopolitics. Q4 turned positive. Management guides 15-20% export growth in FY27, backed by North American Class 8 recovery and Cummins demand.

segments.name: Non-auto (about 35% of mix)
segments.commentary: Includes wind energy, aerospace (GE, HAL, Skyroads), railways and defence. Management said non-auto margins run 100-200 bps above automotive, with shorter working capital cycles.

segments.name: Product mix FY26
segments.commentary: Fasteners 40-42% of revenue; pumps and assemblies, cast and machine assemblies 25-27%; cold extruded and sinter metal about 15%; hot forged and machine components 12%; balance other including radiator caps.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit revenue growth over the next two years; FY27 segment guidance is OE about 13%, retail about 15%, exports 15-20%, implying about 15% overall growth.

Commercial vehicle market growth seen at 4-6% and passenger vehicles at 4-6% in FY27 by analysts; management expects to outperform by 2-3 percentage points, with CV about 8%, PV about 10%, tractors 6-7%.
Class 8 trucks in North America expected to grow at least 10-15% in CY2026 after EPA 2027 norms take effect 1 January 2027; Q1 preliminary Class 8 orders were almost double year-ago.
Management expects UK interest rate cuts in 2026 to help the UK commercial vehicle market.
Railways: current run rate INR 2-3 crore per month, targeting about INR 100 crore per annum, with ramp-up expected by Q3-Q4 FY27; hit rate about 20%.
Wind energy fasteners: next expansion phase to take monthly output from INR 30-35 crore to INR 50 crore.
Raw materials expected to remain stable in the next quarter; nickel, aluminium and copper increases are indexed and passed through to customers.
capex_capacity: Capex of not less than INR 300 crore each year; 25-30% for replacement and about 70% for customer-driven revenue growth.
Wind energy fastener capacity expansion in the next phase, from INR 30-35 crore to INR 50 crore per month.
Aerospace fasteners expansion undertaken to grow alongside customers including GE, HAL and Skyroads.
Power costs reduced through RE power investments and power exchange purchases at lower clearing prices.
demand_pricing: Order books described as full, with new orders coming in; management says it is the first choice for customers in many product developments.

Raw material inflation in nickel and aluminium since the West Asia conflict; management says RM costs have been broadly stable, with pass-through contracts in OE and export pricing set by market conditions in aftermarket.
EV programmes downsized: GM cut EV projections by 50% and Stellantis postponed programmes. Management says ICE and PHEV orders are recovering; full ramp-up expected by 2027.
Company holds about INR 4,000 crore of EV orders (per analyst question; management did not dispute the figure).
Management reports gaining small car share as small players struggle with supply; small car segment recovered after GST rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioning for EV and supply chain risks, and what differentiates it?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharathan said the company leads in ICE and has EV orders with major Indian OEMs, and that electrification is not an immediate threat in high-horsepower, power generation and marine segments. Differentiators cited were quality, brand and first-choice status in developments.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation prioritised and how are margins protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said dividends are 30% of PAT and capex is at least INR 300 crore a year, with 70% for growth. Raw material changes are passed through contractually in OE and by credit notes; export contracts have no pass-through obligation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-auto roadmap, and how does its cash flow and profitability differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh said non-auto includes wind, aerospace, railways and defence, with railways at INR 2-3 crore per month targeting INR 100 crore per annum. Non-auto margins are 100-200 bps higher, with shorter working capital cycles. Non-auto is about 35% of mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export share target of 50% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh said 50% is an aspiration; visibility points to a return to 30-35% export share from new customers and programmes.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment and industry growth expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharathan gave OE 13%, retail 15% and exports 20%, about 15% overall. Company expects to outperform industry by 2-3 percentage points in every segment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin dip QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said the dip reflected RM and direct material inflation after the West Asia conflict, with no other specific cause; full-year margins were described as okay.

qa_highlights.question: How do three-year growth and returns compare with management expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Kumar said the target is nominal GDP plus 2% (about 12-13%) for business planning. Exports and some investments did not perform to plan, but cycles were expected to turn after GST 2.0.

risks_watch: EV programme downsizing at GM and Stellantis, and postponed programmes, could weigh on export volumes.
Raw material inflation in nickel and aluminium since the West Asia conflict; pass-through is contractual in OE but not in exports.
Export share fell about 8% in FY26; Q4 recovery and Class 8 pre-buy need to be sustained, and EPA 2027 warranty issues remain open.
Railway hit rate (about 20%) and qualification timelines for direct participation.
Exceptional items: impairment reversal, MTM on investments and Labour Code gratuity provision of INR 11 crore affect reported PAT comparability.
Exchange gains from rupee weakness contributed to Q4 other income; quality of earnings should be checked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic OE and retail growth and on the export recovery, backed by specific Class 8 and Cummins data. Cautious on EVs and raw materials, and evasive on the 50% export share aspiration and on the 3-year growth benchmark, which management answered in general terms.
key_quotes: And as far as exports is concerned, I think we are back to FY '25 and in line with our budgets.
The management looks at it as the minimum growth that we should target is, let us say, at least a nominal GDP and plus 2%.
So the Class 8 segment is looking up now.

adds.what: Wind energy fastener capacity expansion: monthly output from INR 30-35 crore to INR 50 crore
Railway fasteners ramp-up toward INR 100 crore per annum run-rate (from INR 2-3 crore per month)

growth.why: Management guides about 15% FY27 growth (OE ~13%, retail ~15%, exports 15-20%) and double-digit growth over two years, backed by full order books and a wind expansion (INR 30-35 cr to 50 cr monthly) and a railway ramp-up, but no quantified capacity or order values tie the overall guide together.
